name: United Kingdom

choices.relief: Relief at source (most personal and many workplace pensions)

items.label: Pension contribution (gross)
items.note: Your contribution as a percentage of salary, before any tax relief.

items.label: Pay for income tax
items.note: Net pay and salary sacrifice contributions come off before income tax.

items.label: Pay for National Insurance
items.note: Only salary sacrifice reduces the pay National Insurance and student loans are worked out on.

items.label: Personal allowance
items.note: Withdrawn by £1 for every £2 of income over £100,000, which is what creates the 60% effective band up to £125,140. The £100,000 taper is measured on adjusted net income, which pension contributions reduce.

items.label: Income tax
items.note: Thresholds are on taxable income, i.e. after the personal allowance.

items.label: National Insurance
items.note: Class 1 employee contributions, charged on gross pay rather than taxable income. Weekly thresholds of £241.73 and £966.73 are £12,570 and £50,270 a year.

brackets: Primary threshold to upper earnings limit

items.label: Student loan repayment
items.note: 9% of earnings above the plan's yearly threshold: Plan 1 £26,900, Plan 2 £29,385, Plan 4 £33,795, Plan 5 £25,000. Collected through PAYE alongside tax.

items.label: Postgraduate loan repayment
items.note: 6% of earnings above £21,000, on top of any undergraduate plan.

items.label: Pension contribution
items.note: With relief at source you pay 80% of the contribution and your pension provider claims the other 20% from HMRC; higher and additional rate taxpayers can claim more back through self assessment, which isn't included here. Net pay and salary sacrifice contributions are taken in full, before tax.

assumptions: Standard tax code (1257L) and personal allowance
Employment income only, paid evenly through the year
No student or postgraduate loan unless one is chosen; repayments worked out on the year's earnings, where payroll works per pay period
No pension contribution unless one is entered
notModelled: Tax codes other than the standard personal allowance
Benefits in kind, salary sacrifice and taxable expenses
Blind person's allowance, marriage allowance and other reliefs
Extra relief on relief-at-source pensions for higher-rate taxpayers (claimed through self assessment)
Employer pension contributions, and auto-enrolment's qualifying earnings band (contributions are a percentage of the whole salary)

tests.note: Below the £25,000 Plan 5 threshold: nothing to repay.
Salary sacrifice: tax and NI both on 38,000; NI 8% x 25,430 = 2,034.40.
Relief at source: tax 20% x 27,430 = 5,486 and NI 2,194.40 on the full salary; you pay 80% of 2,000 = 1,600. Same take-home as net pay for a basic-rate taxpayer.
Contribution 11,000 brings adjusted net income to 99,000, under the £100,000 taper, so the full 12,570 allowance stays.
Salary sacrifice also lowers student loan pay: 9% x (38,000 - 29,385) = 775.35.
